requirements.text: Implement `get_track_by_isrc` in the Subsonic driver so tracks can be retrieved by ISRC.
requirements.inference: The issue title directly requests this driver behavior; the stated exact-match use case provides context, not an additional constraint.

requirements.text: The implementation must conform to the (Open) Subsonic specification.
requirements.inference: The repository owner says the idea is acceptable if it conforms to the specification and states they have to stick to the specification. This is a constraint on the requested implementation.

environment: Subsonic driver; the discussion refers to the OpenSubsonic specification.
The stated use case is matching Spotify tracks to Subsonic tracks using ISRCs, potentially avoiding MusicBrainz requests when Subsonic tracks are properly tagged.
prior_attempts: The owner reports that the core-package Subsonic mapper was updated to include an ISRC when present in the server response; the owner says `get_track_by_isrc` was left unchanged because no direct ISRC endpoint was identified.

The request author suggested using `search3` with the ISRC as a query, possibly with a warning, but also considered waiting for more specific API support. The owner said they would look into it; the discussion does not establish that this workaround was adopted or implemented.
missing_information: The discussion does not establish whether a specification-supported ISRC lookup API becomes available, whether the proposed `search3` workaround is accepted, or whether the requested lookup has since been implemented.

output.reason: The requested behavior is narrowly defined: accept an ISRC, retrieve the matching Subsonic track, and conform to the (Open)Subsonic specification (r0, r1). The discussion leaves the decisive implementation question unresolved: whether querying `search3` with an ISRC is an acceptable specification-conforming lookup or whether a more specific API is needed (q2, q3, q4). Without that, a reuse search has no established advantage over a small driver-level change.

direct_alternative.description: Use the existing Subsonic client to search for the ISRC, then return only a track whose mapped ISRC exactly matches; alternatively, use a specification-supported lookup if one exists.
limitations: The supplied discussion does not establish that the search workaround is acceptable or specification-conforming (q2, q4).
The target sample contains no implementation source, so existing driver behavior and available client methods are unverified.
The discussion does not establish whether a more specific lookup API is available or whether the request has since been implemented (q4).

output.benefit_hypothesis: A reusable implementation could reduce bespoke Subsonic lookup logic, but no concrete incremental advantage over the direct driver-level approach is established until the supported lookup behavior is clarified.
output.benefit_test: First establish the specification-conforming lookup behavior. Then compare any candidate implementation with the direct driver-level approach on exact ISRC matching, returned-track correctness, and conformance; investigate reuse only if it provides a measurable advantage without violating the specification.
